hero.title: ImpAct-Climate Micro-Grants
hero.description: Empowering colleges and institutes across Canada to lead climate action through innovative, community-driven projects. Explore the impact of micro-grant funded initiatives tackling waste, energy, biodiversity, and more.
hero.imageAlt: Aerial view of lush Canadian forest representing climate action

storytelling.headline: Driving Change Across Canada
storytelling.paragraph1: Through the ImpAct-Climate Micro-Grants program, colleges and institutes across Canada are transforming how their communities respond to the climate crisis. From innovative waste reduction strategies to groundbreaking biodiversity projects, these initiatives are creating real, measurable change.
storytelling.paragraph2: Each funded project represents a unique partnership between students, faculty, and community members working together to build a more sustainable future. The results speak for themselves — reduced emissions, restored ecosystems, and empowered communities.
storytelling.paragraph3: This program demonstrates that meaningful climate action starts at the local level, with institutions that are deeply connected to the communities they serve.
storytelling.quote: "These micro-grants have been a catalyst for change — empowering our students to become the climate leaders of tomorrow."

about.heroSubtitle: Learn more about CICan and the ImpAct-Climate Micro-Grants program.
about.missionP1: As part of the final year of the ImpAct-Climate project, CICan launched the Micro-Grant initiative to maximize impact and extend the reach of project outcomes across the college and institute sector. Through this initiative, participating institutions received up to $8,000 to design and deliver campus-based activities focused on raising awareness, encouraging behaviour change, and contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction.
about.missionP2: The Micro-Grants were designed to enable rapid, practical action by empowering institutions to test ideas, engage students and staff, and pilot solutions that could be scaled or adapted over time. Projects were required to include a strong awareness component, demonstrate potential for GHG reduction, and incorporate community engagement, often through public events or campaigns.
about.missionP3: Positioned as a targeted “top-up” in the project’s final phase, the initiative helped activate new participants while reinforcing momentum among engaged institutions. By supporting locally driven initiatives within a national framework, the Micro-Grant program fostered collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovation, contributing to broader climate goals and strengthening institutional capacity for sustained action.
about.missionP4: The ImpAct-Climate project recognized that meaningful climate action must be grounded in diverse ways of knowing, including Indigenous perspectives, leadership, and approaches to sustainability.
about.missionP5: Through the Micro-Grant initiative and broader project activities, participating colleges and institutes were encouraged to meaningfully engage Indigenous communities, knowledge holders, and learners in the design and delivery of climate initiatives. This included incorporating Indigenous knowledge systems, supporting participation of Elders and Knowledge Keepers, and creating space for community-led dialogue and learning.
about.missionP6: These efforts helped strengthen relationships between institutions and Indigenous communities while reinforcing the importance of holistic, place-based approaches to climate action. They also contributed to a deeper understanding that sustainability is not only an environmental objective, but a cultural, social, and relational responsibility.
